emulators.name: 8bitworkshop
emulators.blurb: A browser IDE that compiles C, assembly and Verilog and runs the result instantly on emulated 8-bit computers, consoles and a Verilog simulator.
emulators.why: Write a 6809 or Z80 program and see it running on the emulated target with a debugger, or simulate Verilog hardware without a toolchain.
can: compile C and assembly in browser
emulators.ease_note: Pick a platform and example; builds and runs at once.

emulators.name: a2 (Apple ][+)
emulators.blurb: David Caldwell's compact WebGL-accelerated Apple ][+ emulator.
emulators.why: A quick no-frills II+ with joystick mode, useful when you just want a plain Apple II without extras.
emulators.ease_note: Bare page with few instructions.

emulators.name: Academo Amplitude Modulation
emulators.blurb: Shows a carrier, a modulating wave and their product with audio, revealing that modulating amplitude produces sum and difference tones.
emulators.why: A minimal AM demo that connects modulation to sidebands, a stepping stone to understanding DSB and SSB.
emulators.ease_note: Three sliders and a sound toggle

emulators.name: Academo Lissajous Curves
emulators.blurb: Adjust amplitudes, frequency ratio and phase to draw Lissajous curves as an X-Y oscilloscope would.
emulators.why: Lissajous patterns are the classic way to compare two frequencies or measure phase on a scope, still useful for calibrating oscillators.
emulators.ease_note: Five sliders

emulators.name: Academo Spectrum Analyzer
emulators.blurb: Spectrogram demo with preset sounds (modem, siren, whale, violin) plus your own audio files, with a switchable log or linear frequency axis.
emulators.why: The modem and siren presets show FSK/PSK-like sounds and chirps in the frequency domain, exactly what you see on a digital-mode waterfall.
can: play preset sounds and watch their spectra
emulators.ease_note: Press play on a preset

emulators.name: Academo Virtual Oscilloscope
emulators.blurb: A browser oscilloscope with a built-in sine/square generator or live microphone input and real scope controls for time base, gain and offset.
emulators.why: Teaches how to read a scope before touching a real one, and lets you view your audio chain's waveform without hardware.
can: display a tone generator or the microphone
emulators.ease_note: Works immediately; mic mode needs Chrome

emulators.name: Academo Wave Interference and Beat Frequency
emulators.blurb: Overlays two sine waves and their sum with sound so you can see and hear beats when the frequencies are close.
emulators.why: Beats are how you zero-beat a CW signal or a calibrator; this shows why the wobble rate equals the frequency difference.
emulators.ease_note: Two sliders

emulators.name: ACO Simulator (Thiago Ferreira)
emulators.blurb: Visual ant colony optimization solving TSP instances with pheromone trails you can watch evaporate and reinforce.
emulators.why: Shows stigmergy in action: tune alpha, beta and evaporation and see the colony converge on short tours.
emulators.ease_note: Load an example and press start; parameters are optional.

emulators.name: Altair 8800 Simulator (s2js)
emulators.blurb: A JavaScript Altair 8800 with clicking switches, fan noise, a 2 MHz 8080 and a simulated ASR-33 teletype that loads the original 1975 Microsoft BASIC from paper tape.
emulators.why: The closest browser experience to bootstrapping a real Altair: toggle in the bootloader, load BASIC at 110 baud and hear the teletype.
emulators.ease_note: Runs instantly; the guided tutorial walks you through toggling and loading BASIC.

emulators.name: An Interactive Introduction to Fourier Transforms (Jez Swanson)
emulators.blurb: A scroll-through explorable that decomposes drawn waves, doodles and sounds into sine components with sliders and epicycle animations.
emulators.why: The gentlest correct intuition for why any signal is a sum of sines; ideal first stop before reading about spectra, filters or SSB.
can: draw a wave and see its sine components
see how JPEG uses frequency components
emulators.ease_note: Plain web page, no setup

emulators.name: AntennaSim (EA1FUO)
emulators.blurb: Open-source NEC2 antenna simulator compiled to WebAssembly with 17 templates, a wire editor, 3-D pattern viewer, SWR/impedance charts and an optimizer.
emulators.why: An EZNEC-style modeller that runs on a phone or tablet, letting hams model dipoles, verticals and Yagis without installing anything.
can: load antenna templates or edit wires
emulators.ease_note: Templates make it easy; custom geometry needs NEC knowledge

emulators.name: Apple 1js
emulators.blurb: Will Scullin's JavaScript emulation of the 1976 Apple I with the Woz Monitor and Integer BASIC.
emulators.why: Type into the Woz Monitor exactly as Wozniak intended; a lovely minimal demonstration of where personal computing started.
can: paste in hex or BASIC programs
emulators.ease_note: Boots to the monitor prompt; you need to know a couple of monitor commands.

emulators.name: Apple ][js / Apple //jse
emulators.blurb: Will Scullin's long-established Apple II emulator in TypeScript with colour graphics, sound, disk drives and a built-in disk catalogue; the /apple//e page is the IIe version.
emulators.why: Boots to Applesoft BASIC with a menu of public-domain and freely licensed disks, works well on phones and tablets, and has a companion IIe build at scullinsteel.com/apple//e.
emulators.ease_note: Just loads to the BASIC prompt with a disk menu.

emulators.name: Apple2TS
emulators.blurb: Chris Torrence's TypeScript Apple IIe emulator with a debugger, Mockingboard sound, joystick and built-in sample disks.
emulators.why: Modern, actively developed, and includes a very good debugger and disassembler, so it is useful for learning 6502 assembly as well as running old disks.
emulators.ease_note: Boots immediately with a clear toolbar.

emulators.name: Archimedes Live!
emulators.blurb: Paul Stone's WebAssembly port of Arculator that boots RISC OS in the browser with a library of games and demos.
emulators.why: The first ARM-based desktop computer, complete with the RISC OS desktop and !Edit/!Draw, runnable with a click; a must for anyone interested in ARM history.
can: drag in disc images or archives
emulators.ease_note: Boots to the RISC OS desktop with a software menu.

emulators.name: ARMlite
emulators.blurb: Peter Higginson's browser simulator for a simplified ARM assembly language with a memory-mapped pixel display, aimed at schools.
emulators.why: A friendly step up from Little Man Computer into real-looking ARM code, with visual output and single-stepping.
emulators.ease_note: Load a sample and press run.

emulators.name: ASM80 online IDE and emulators
emulators.blurb: A browser IDE with assemblers for eight 8-bit CPUs and built-in emulators for several single-board and hobby machines.
emulators.why: Assemble 6809, Z80, 8080 or 1802 code and run it on an emulated KIM-1, CP/M or SBC target without leaving the browser.
emulators.ease_note: Free but a full IDE; you need to pick a target and know its conventions.

emulators.name: AtariOnline (jsA8E)
emulators.blurb: A hosted version of the jsA8E Atari 800XL emulator with ready-made pages for Atari BASIC, Logo, Assembler Editor, MAC/65 and FastBasic.
emulators.why: Lets you program a real Atari 8-bit in the browser with the classic development tools already mounted; ideal for retro coding sessions.
emulators.ease_note: Pick a page and it boots; no sound in the emulator core.

emulators.name: Ben Eater's 8-bit Computer Simulation
emulators.blurb: A browser simulation of Ben Eater's famous breadboard 8-bit computer with hex program entry, an assembler and example programs.
emulators.why: Try the Fibonacci and multiplication programs from the video series before (or instead of) building the 44 breadboards.
emulators.ease_note: Pick an example and press Run.

emulators.name: BetterExplained Fourier Transform simulator
emulators.blurb: The embedded simulator from Kalid Azad's Interactive Guide to the Fourier Transform lets you type a time pattern or cycle recipe and see the other domain instantly.
emulators.why: Explains the DFT as a smoothie recipe of cycles, a good mental model for reading a waterfall or band scope.
can: type time samples and get cycles
emulators.ease_note: Type values into the box

emulators.name: Bifurcation Diagram of the Logistic Map
emulators.blurb: Interactive bifurcation diagram where you click-drag to zoom into period-doubling cascades, plus time-series and final-state plots.
emulators.why: Zooming into the diagram reveals its self-similar structure and Feigenbaum scaling; offset and limit controls let you tune the plot density.
emulators.ease_note: Drag a box to zoom, nothing else needed

emulators.name: BK-0010/0011M Online Emulator (BkMacro)
emulators.blurb: Ufasoft's HTML5 emulator of the Soviet PDP-11-compatible BK-0010 and BK-0011M home computers.
emulators.why: The BK was the USSR's most popular home computer and runs a 16-bit PDP-11 instruction set; drop in a .bin or disk image and it runs.
emulators.ease_note: Boots on load but the page is Russian/English mixed and assumes you know the machine.

emulators.name: Blochy Bloch Sphere Simulator
emulators.blurb: Simulate a qubit or spin-1/2 on the Bloch sphere with gates, custom-axis rotations and pulse sequences.
emulators.why: Clean visual of how Pauli, Hadamard and phase gates rotate a state; also handy for NMR/ESR-style pulse intuition and presentation figures.
emulators.ease_note: Click and run

emulators.name: Boids (Ben Eater)
emulators.blurb: Ben Eater's minimal boids page with sliders for coherence, separation, alignment and visual range, plus a path-trace toggle.
emulators.why: The clearest introduction to Reynolds' three rules: switch each one off individually and watch the flock fall apart.
emulators.ease_note: Runs immediately.

emulators.name: Buddhabrot Renderer (KilledByAPixel)
emulators.blurb: Frank Force's JavaScript HD Buddhabrot renderer that accumulates over time up to 7680x4320 output.
emulators.why: Leave it running in a tab and it keeps refining; toggle Anti-Buddhabrot, greyscale or symmetric modes and save the PNG whenever it looks good.
emulators.ease_note: Press start and wait; a few obvious sliders

emulators.name: Buddhabrot WebGPU Explorer
emulators.blurb: WebGPU-accelerated Buddhabrot renderer that accumulates escape orbits on the GPU.
emulators.why: Buddhabrot is normally painfully slow to render; doing it on the GPU makes the ghostly nebula image emerge in seconds.
emulators.ease_note: Requires a WebGPU browser; minimal UI

emulators.name: BullGammaTor (Bull Gamma 3)
emulators.blurb: An Angular/JavaScript emulator of the French 1952 Bull Gamma 3 tube calculator with drum extension, backed by the ACONIT computing-history association.
emulators.why: A rare chance to program a first-generation European machine with its plugboard-era instruction set (French UI).
emulators.ease_note: French interface and unusual machine; needs the ACONIT documentation.

emulators.name: C64 JavaScript Emulator (Tanja's C64)
emulators.blurb: A WebAssembly cross-compile of Thomas Hochgoetz's C++ C64 emulator with keyboard, touch and gamepad input.
emulators.why: A long-running independent C64 emulator that runs in the browser with no setup; handy as a second opinion when a program misbehaves elsewhere.
emulators.ease_note: Starts immediately; site navigation is slightly cluttered.

emulators.name: Celestia Web
emulators.blurb: The classic Celestia space simulator compiled to run in the browser, letting you travel anywhere in a real-time 3-D universe.
emulators.why: Free-flight through a physically positioned solar system and star catalog without installing the desktop app.
can: fly to planets, moons and stars
emulators.ease_note: Large WebAssembly download on first load

emulators.name: Cellula
emulators.blurb: A one-stop cellular automata playground covering Life-like rulestrings, Brian's Brain, Wireworld, Langton's ant, elementary rules and continuous neural automata.
emulators.why: Handy when you want to compare many classic automata in one UI with editable rulestrings and neighbourhoods rather than opening a different site for each.
emulators.ease_note: Pick an automaton from the menu; epilepsy warning for flashing rules.

emulators.name: CEM Sim (Maxwell FDTD in the browser)
emulators.blurb: GPU-accelerated finite-difference time-domain Maxwell solver where you draw materials and sources and watch fields evolve.
emulators.why: A real computational-EM method (FDTD) made interactive: set permittivity, permeability and conductivity and see reflection, refraction and loss.
can: draw materials with permittivity and conductivity
emulators.ease_note: Works in browser; needs WebGL and a little explanation

emulators.name: Chaos Game (MathsBot)
emulators.blurb: Classroom-style chaos game that plots points halfway to random triangle vertices until the Sierpinski triangle appears.
emulators.why: The cleanest demonstration of how randomness produces order; ideal for showing students or kids.
emulators.ease_note: One button, one setting

emulators.name: Chladni Patterns (dynamicmath.xyz)
emulators.blurb: Juan Carlos Ponce Campuzano's particle simulation of sand gathering on the nodal lines of square and circular vibrating plates.
emulators.why: Sweep the mode numbers and frequency to see sand assemble into Chladni figures, with a 3D view of the underlying wave.
emulators.ease_note: Applets run inline; drag sliders.

emulators.name: Chrome Music Lab: Spectrogram
emulators.blurb: Google's polished scrolling spectrogram of your microphone or preset sounds, rendered in 3-D with a single tap.
emulators.why: The fastest way to show a beginner what a waterfall display is and to look at the harmonics in your own voice or a CW sidetone.
can: visualise the microphone in real time
play preset sounds (flute, harp, whistle, modem)
emulators.ease_note: One tap, allow microphone

emulators.name: CircuitLab
emulators.blurb: A browser schematic editor and SPICE-style simulator with DC, transient and frequency-domain analysis and Bode plots.
emulators.why: Closer to LTspice than the animated sims: proper AC sweeps and plots for filter and amplifier design, straight from a schematic.
emulators.ease_note: Editor opens freely but saving and extended use need an account or subscription.

emulators.name: CircuitVerse
emulators.blurb: An open-source online digital logic simulator with gates, flip-flops, ALUs, displays and sub-circuits, plus Verilog export.
emulators.why: Build and share digital designs (counters, decoders, a small CPU) with a friendly editor; free and open source.
emulators.ease_note: Simulator opens without login; save requires an account.

emulators.name: CloudpilotEmu (Palm OS)
emulators.blurb: A web-based Palm OS emulator derived from POSE that supports more than 30 Palm, Sony and Handera devices, running entirely client-side.
emulators.why: Install PRC apps, use HotSync-free file import and keep continuous state saves in your browser; requires a ROM image dumped from your own device.
emulators.ease_note: Works well once you supply a Palm ROM; nothing runs without one.

emulators.name: CloudT (TRS-80 Model 100)
emulators.blurb: The Bitchin100 community's Model 100 emulator running as a browser progressive web app.
emulators.why: The Model 100 was the classic field notebook for hams and journalists; CloudT gives you its BASIC, TEXT and TELCOM menu on any device, even offline.
emulators.ease_note: Boots to the familiar menu; documentation lives on the Bitchin100 wiki.

emulators.name: Collatz Graph (Jason Davies)
emulators.blurb: D3 radial tree of Collatz orbits, filterable by orbit length with a slider.
emulators.why: A small but elegant way to see the Collatz tree structure grow as you allow longer orbits.
emulators.ease_note: One slider

emulators.name: Compiler Explorer (godbolt)
emulators.blurb: Matt Godbolt's site that compiles source code with hundreds of compilers and shows the generated assembly, with an execution option.
emulators.why: Not an emulator of a machine, but the fastest way to see what real compilers emit for AVR, ARM or RISC-V, and to run the output.
emulators.ease_note: Type code, pick a compiler, done.

emulators.name: Complex Function Plotter (Samuel Li)
emulators.blurb: Smooth WebGL domain-colouring plotter for complex functions parameterised by any number of variables.
emulators.why: Type an expression and drag its parameters to watch zeros and poles move in real time; a favourite for complex-analysis intuition.
emulators.ease_note: Expression box plus sliders; needs WebGL

emulators.name: ContrAltoJS Xerox Alto Emulator
emulators.blurb: A JavaScript port of the Living Computer Museum's ContrAlto emulator that runs original Xerox Alto disk images, including Smalltalk-76 and games, in the browser.
emulators.why: See the 1973 machine that invented the GUI and the mouse-driven desktop, and even play networked Alto games via WebRTC.
emulators.ease_note: Choose a disk and boot; Alto Executive commands take a little learning.

emulators.name: Convolution Demo (phiresky)
emulators.blurb: React/TypeScript demo that animates the convolution of two selectable functions entirely in the browser.
emulators.why: Convolution is what every filter does to a signal; seeing the flip-and-slide integral makes impulse responses intuitive.
emulators.ease_note: Loads and animates immediately

emulators.name: Convolution Demo and Visualization (Erik Cheever, Swarthmore)
emulators.blurb: Three-graph JavaScript tool that walks through graphical convolution, showing f(λ), the flipped and shifted h(t−λ), their product and the running integral.
emulators.why: Part of a full linear-systems tutorial, so the visual is backed by worked explanations of impulse response and system behaviour.
can: drag t and watch the overlap
emulators.ease_note: Works instantly; academic layout

emulators.name: copy.sh Game of Life
emulators.blurb: A fast, infinite-grid Conway's Game of Life in pure JavaScript built on the HashLife algorithm, with a large library of famous patterns.
emulators.why: The go-to place to watch monsters like the Tetris processor, Gemini and Caterpillar run at millions of generations per second without installing Golly. Pattern-by-URL makes it trivial to link a specific construction.
emulators.ease_note: Open the page and press play; patterns load from a dropdown or URL.

emulators.name: CPCBox
emulators.blurb: The classic JavaScript Amstrad CPC emulator CPCBox, hosted with a selection of demos and games.
emulators.why: Boots to Locomotive BASIC on any of the three CPC models and remains one of the best-known browser CPCs.
emulators.ease_note: Official CPCBox site; it shows a short bot check before the emulator loads.

emulators.name: CPUlator
emulators.blurb: A full-system educational CPU simulator with assembler, debugger and memory-mapped I/O devices for ARM, MIPS, RISC-V and Nios II.
emulators.why: Arguably the best free debugger for learning assembly: breakpoints, watchpoints, reverse stepping and calling-convention checks, all in a tab.
emulators.ease_note: Choose an architecture, paste code, compile and run; lots of panels but well labelled.

emulators.name: Critically Inflammatory (Complexity Explorables)
emulators.blurb: The Drossel-Schwabl forest fire model as an explorable: trees grow, lightning strikes, and fire sizes become scale-free.
emulators.why: A clean demonstration of self-organized criticality and its link to epidemics, with just three sliders.
emulators.ease_note: Press play.

emulators.name: CURTA simulator in SVG (Robert Cailliau)
emulators.blurb: Robert Cailliau's plug-in-free SVG/JavaScript simulation of the Curta Type II mechanical calculator, with draggable sliders, crank and carriage.
emulators.why: Operate a Curta exactly as you would the real thing (including ten's-complement subtraction and shifted multiplication) without paying collector prices.
emulators.ease_note: Works instantly, but you need to know the Curta procedure to compute.

emulators.name: CurtaGL 3D Curta calculator (Jon Millen)
emulators.blurb: A Blender-modelled, Unity-built WebGL Curta Type I you can turn, set and clear with mouse or touch.
emulators.why: A polished 3D interactive Curta based on the VCalc.net plans, good for demonstrating how the machine is operated.
emulators.ease_note: Unity WebGL build is heavy and served over plain HTTP.

emulators.name: DeepMandelbrot
emulators.blurb: WebGL Mandelbrot/Julia explorer that uses perturbation theory to keep zooming far past double-precision limits.
emulators.why: One of the fastest browser deep zoomers around; you can dive to absurd depths in real time with smooth colouring and supersampling, plus some tongue-in-cheek tessellation colour modes.
emulators.ease_note: Open and scroll to zoom; a small settings panel for colouring and quality

emulators.name: Derek's Virtual Slide Rule Gallery
emulators.blurb: Derek Ross's classic JavaScript simulations of seven Pickett slide rules, draggable with the mouse, plus a calculations-by-example tutorial.
emulators.why: The original web slide rules, ideal for learning C/D/A/B scale technique on the same models that flew on Apollo (N600-ES).
emulators.ease_note: Pick a rule and drag; mouse only, no touch support.

emulators.name: DigitalJS Online
emulators.blurb: A web front end that synthesises your Verilog (via Yosys) and simulates the resulting netlist interactively with clickable inputs and waveforms.
emulators.why: Write SystemVerilog, click Synthesize and poke the gate-level schematic; a great bridge between HDL and logic sims.
emulators.ease_note: Paste Verilog and press Synthesize (synthesis runs on the server, simulation in browser).

emulators.name: Domain Coloring Tools (dynamicmath.xyz)
emulators.blurb: Juan Carlos Ponce Campuzano's suite of domain-colouring plotters in JavaScript and WebGL with HSB/HSL/HSLuv, discrete and smooth schemes.
emulators.why: Several colouring conventions side by side and a gallery of classic functions make it good for both teaching and pretty pictures.
emulators.ease_note: Choose a tool, type a function

emulators.name: DOSBox in the browser (Retro Game Coders)
emulators.blurb: A minimal js-dos page that boots straight to a DOS C:\ prompt so you can try DOS commands without setting anything up.
emulators.why: The simplest possible 'DOS prompt in a tab' for demonstrating DOS to newcomers.
emulators.ease_note: Loads directly to C:\.

emulators.name: Double Pendulum (myPhysicsLab)
emulators.blurb: Erik Neumann's Runge-Kutta double pendulum with draggable bobs, adjustable masses and lengths, and graph views.
emulators.why: Drag the pendulum to a new start, release, and watch chaos; the time-graph and phase views make sensitive dependence tangible.
can: drag the pendulum to set initial state
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load; drag the bobs.

emulators.name: Drawerings
emulators.blurb: Free HTML5 mandala and kaleidoscope drawing tool with a shareable community gallery.
emulators.why: Instant meditative doodling: every stroke is mirrored radially, and finished drawings can be shared or browsed in the gallery.
emulators.ease_note: Open the draw page and start drawing

emulators.name: EarLevel Biquad Calculator v3
emulators.blurb: Nigel Redmon's in-page calculator produces biquad coefficients for low/high/band-pass, notch, shelf and peak filters and plots magnitude and phase live; it also graphs any coefficients you paste in.
emulators.why: Gives ready-to-use coefficients for DSP audio filters in an SDR or digital-mode project and shows the response before you code it.
can: select filter type, Fc, Q and gain
emulators.ease_note: Type values, plot updates

emulators.name: EarLevel Pole-Zero Placement v2
emulators.blurb: JavaScript remake of the classic applet: set pole and zero magnitude and angle on the unit circle and see the resulting frequency response.
emulators.why: The quickest way to internalise 'poles blow, zeros suck' and how z-plane placement shapes notches and resonances.
can: switch linear and log response display
emulators.ease_note: Four sliders

emulators.name: Easy 6502
emulators.blurb: Nick Morgan's interactive 6502 assembly tutorial with an embedded assembler, simulator, debugger and a tiny pixel display.
emulators.why: The gentlest introduction to 6502 assembly anywhere; ends with a working Snake game you can single-step.
emulators.ease_note: Click Assemble then Run in the first example; nothing to configure.

emulators.name: Elementary Cellular Automaton Simulator (celldemo)
emulators.blurb: A minimal scrolling explorer for all 256 Wolfram elementary rules with a clickable next-state rule table.
emulators.why: The quickest way to build a rule bit by bit and see the pattern scroll past; presets link to explanations of the famous rules.
emulators.ease_note: Click rule cells and watch; nothing to configure.

emulators.name: ElkJS
emulators.blurb: Darren Coles's JavaScript Acorn Electron emulator ported from Elkulator with a UEF file browser.
emulators.why: A dedicated Electron with Plus 1/Plus 3 style expansion options; boots to BBC BASIC so you can type in listings from old magazines.
emulators.ease_note: Boots to BASIC; you supply your own tape images.

emulators.name: Emergent Mind Elementary CA Explorer
emulators.blurb: A gallery of all 256 elementary rules you can flip through with the arrow keys, with noteworthy rules highlighted and the four Wolfram classes explained.
emulators.why: Best for browsing: see a thumbnail of every rule at once and read why 30, 90 and 110 matter without any setup.
emulators.ease_note: Click a rule number; instant.

emulators.name: Emoji Simulator (Nicky Case)
emulators.blurb: Nicky Case's re-launched emoji cellular automata builder: draw with emoji, define neighbour rules, and share simulations by link.
emulators.why: The friendliest rule editor around; you can build forest fires, epidemics or Life with emoji and share a URL, no code required.
emulators.ease_note: Pick an example and press play.

emulators.name: Emulator of Russian calculators (Elektronika MK-61 and friends)
emulators.blurb: A browser emulator of the Soviet Elektronika programmable calculator family (MK-61, B3-34, MK-54, MK-56) plus a Felix arithmometer and Russian slide rule and abacus, with register and program views.
emulators.why: The MK-61 has a cult following for its undocumented 'eggog' behaviour and games; this page lets you enter and run those programs with visible stack and program counter.
emulators.ease_note: Interface is in Russian but the calculator keys are self-explanatory.

emulators.name: Eschersketch
emulators.blurb: Anselm Levskaya's drawing program for the 17 wallpaper groups and rosette point groups, with live repeating layout and PNG/SVG export.
emulators.why: Draw one stroke and see it tiled under any plane symmetry group; exports hi-res seamless tiles for fabric or print-on-demand.
emulators.ease_note: Draw immediately; symmetry picker takes a moment to learn

emulators.name: EstyJS
emulators.blurb: Darren Coles's Atari ST emulator in JavaScript, shipping with EmuTOS so it boots to the GEM desktop.
emulators.why: A pure JavaScript ST that needs no TOS ROM from you; a quick way to see GEM and try ST software.
can: boots to GEM desktop with EmuTOS
emulators.ease_note: Boots on load; you provide disk images for anything beyond the bundled demos.

emulators.name: EveryCircuit
emulators.blurb: A polished, animated circuit simulator with real-time oscilloscope traces and a large community library of shared circuits.
emulators.why: Beautiful animation of voltages and currents makes it a good teaching tool; the community circuits cover oscillators, amplifiers and radio front ends.
emulators.ease_note: Free tier is limited and you must create an account; needs WebGL.

emulators.name: Falstad 1-D Quantum Mechanics
emulators.blurb: Solves the Schrodinger equation for a particle in 1-D potentials and shows energy levels, wavefunctions, momentum and phase.
emulators.why: The canonical electron-in-a-box explorer: click energy levels, mix states with phasors and watch the probability density evolve.
can: choose infinite well, harmonic and other potentials
emulators.ease_note: Instant, but controls assume some QM background

emulators.name: Falstad 2-D Electrodynamics (EM Wave)
emulators.blurb: A 2-D Maxwell solver showing electric and magnetic fields as waves radiate, reflect off conductors and pass through dielectrics.
emulators.why: See E and B fields together as waves interact with mirrors, lenses, waveguides and dipoles; a direct visual of the physics behind RF propagation.
can: view E-field colors and B-field arrows
emulators.ease_note: Loads instantly; menus are terse

emulators.name: Falstad 3-D Magnetostatic Fields
systems: magnetic fields of wires, loops, solenoids and magnets
emulators.blurb: Rotatable 3-D view of magnetic fields around current-carrying wires, loops, solenoids, toroids and magnets.
emulators.why: Makes the field geometry of coils and toroids tangible with moving field-line particles, plus the vector potential A.
can: select many current and magnet configurations
show field lines, vectors or particles
emulators.ease_note: Runs in browser; page text still mentions the old Java version

emulators.name: Falstad 3-D Waves Applet
emulators.blurb: JS applet showing scalar waves in a rotatable 3-D box from point, line and plane sources with colour-coded pressure and interference between sources.
emulators.why: Extends ripple-tank intuition to three dimensions, handy for picturing spherical wavefronts and source interference in space.
can: rotate the 3-D view with the mouse
emulators.ease_note: Runs immediately; 3-D navigation takes practice

emulators.name: Falstad Analog Filter Applet
emulators.blurb: JS applet that shows the frequency response of sample analog filter circuits with a cutoff slider and a menu of circuit topologies.
emulators.why: Quick intuition for RC, LC, crystal and active filters used in receiver front ends and audio stages.
emulators.ease_note: Slider and menu only

emulators.name: Falstad Antenna Applet
emulators.blurb: JS applet that animates the waves radiated by dipoles, loops and antenna arrays in two dimensions with selectable setups.
emulators.why: Shows in motion how element spacing and phasing create directional radiation, the physics behind Yagis and phased verticals.
can: choose dipole, array and phased-array setups
emulators.ease_note: Setup menu is the main control

emulators.name: Falstad CircuitJS
emulators.blurb: Paul Falstad's animated circuit simulator, now in JavaScript, showing current flow and voltages in real time with a huge library of example circuits.
emulators.why: The hobbyist favourite for understanding oscillators, filters, mixers and amplifiers visually; includes RF-relevant examples like Colpitts and Hartley oscillators and a scope.
emulators.ease_note: Opens with a running LRC circuit; menus are simple.

emulators.name: Falstad CircuitJS: Standing Wave on a Transmission Line
emulators.blurb: A ready-made example in Falstad's circuit simulator where a wave travels down a mis-terminated line and reflects, with the standing wave and doubled voltage visible in the scope traces.
emulators.why: Directly demonstrates what SWR is at the circuit level and links to sibling examples on matched and mismatched termination.
can: watch the wave reflect from the load
edit the termination or line impedance
emulators.ease_note: Loads the example directly; editing needs simulator familiarity

emulators.name: Falstad Digital Filters Applet
emulators.blurb: Interactive JS applet that plots a digital filter's frequency response, impulse response and the live spectrum and waveform of audio passing through it.
emulators.why: Lets you hear and see what a DSP audio or IF filter does to a signal, including ringing and phase effects.
can: choose low/high/band-pass, notch, comb and custom filters
click the response curve to set cutoff
play test signals through the filter
view pole-zero plots for IIR types
emulators.ease_note: Works instantly; menus take a minute to learn

emulators.name: Falstad Fourier Series Applet
emulators.blurb: Paul Falstad's classic JS applet shows a periodic waveform (sine, square, sawtooth, noise or hand-drawn) alongside its harmonic magnitudes and phases, with audio.
emulators.why: Instantly shows why a square wave or key click is rich in harmonics, which is the root of splatter, clicks and bandwidth in transmitters.
can: pick or draw a periodic waveform
edit individual harmonic amplitudes and phases
limit the number of terms to see Gibbs ringing
emulators.ease_note: Loads instantly in any browser

emulators.name: Falstad Gas Molecules Simulation
emulators.blurb: Bouncing molecules colored by kinetic energy with a live velocity histogram showing the Maxwell-Boltzmann shape.
emulators.why: A minimal kinetic-theory demo where you can see the speed distribution settle into its statistical form.
emulators.ease_note: Pick a preset from the menu; the full-screen JavaScript version, the parent page still describes the old Java applet.

emulators.name: Falstad Hydrogen Atom Orbitals
emulators.blurb: Rotatable 3-D display of hydrogen-atom orbitals, switchable between real (chemistry) and complex (physics) forms.
emulators.why: See what s, p, d and f orbitals really look like and animate superpositions to watch the electron cloud oscillate.
can: pick any n, l, m state
emulators.ease_note: Instant; menu-driven

emulators.name: Falstad Math and Physics Applets
emulators.blurb: Paul Falstad's long-running collection of physics and math applets, almost all converted from Java to plain JavaScript.
emulators.why: Dense, no-frills simulations that go deeper than most teaching sims; covers antennas, waveguides, EM waves, filters, Fourier series and quantum states in one place.
can: browse dozens of JS physics sims
emulators.ease_note: Old-school UI but works instantly in the browser

emulators.name: Falstad Ripple Tank
emulators.blurb: WebGL ripple tank where you draw sources, walls and media and watch interference, diffraction, resonance, phased-array steering and Doppler shifts in real time.
emulators.why: The single best sandbox for seeing why antenna arrays form lobes, how slits diffract and what a moving source does to wavelength.
can: load dozens of preset setups including phased arrays
draw walls and media with the mouse
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load; examples menu for quick starts

emulators.name: Filter Playground (Boris Smus)
emulators.blurb: Explorable that lets you build a filter by wizard, transfer-function text or by dragging poles and zeros, then shows a 3-D transfer surface, Bode view and filtered audio.
emulators.why: Bridges the gap between the z-plane picture and what you hear, using the browser's own IIRFilterNode.
can: generate filters from Fc, Q and gain
add and drag poles and zeros
emulators.ease_note: WebGL views; a short read of the intro helps

emulators.name: Firebird (WebAssembly) TI-Nspire emulator
emulators.blurb: The Qt-based Firebird TI-Nspire ARM emulator compiled to WebAssembly and hosted on GitHub Pages.
emulators.why: The only way to run a full TI-Nspire in a browser, useful for testing Lua or Ndless programs; requires boot1/boot2 and OS files dumped from your own calculator.
can: load your own boot and flash images
emulators.ease_note: Needs you to assemble a flash image from your own calculator's boot files and OS before anything runs.

emulators.name: Flock'n Roll (Complexity Explorables)
emulators.blurb: Dirk Brockmann's explorable of Couzin's collective-motion model, where 200 agents form swarms, tori and mills depending on interaction radii.
emulators.why: Shows the phase transitions of flocking (swarm to torus to parallel group) that plain boids demos miss, with blind-spot and wiggle controls.
emulators.ease_note: Press play.

emulators.name: Fluid Dynamics Simulation (Dan Schroeder, Lattice-Boltzmann)
emulators.blurb: A wind-tunnel style lattice-Boltzmann flow sim where you draw barriers and watch velocity, curl and vortex streets.
emulators.why: Semi-quantitative fluid physics you can probe: plot force on a barrier, tracer particles and flowlines, with the algorithm explained on the page.
can: plot speed, curl, density or pressure
emulators.ease_note: Click and run; Chrome recommended

emulators.name: Fluid Particles (David Li)
emulators.blurb: Real-time particle-based 3-D liquid you can pour and stir, rendered entirely in WebGL.
emulators.why: A visually striking 3-D free-surface fluid running on your GPU, good for seeing splashes and sloshing rather than 2-D flow.
emulators.ease_note: Needs a decent GPU; otherwise click and run

emulators.name: Fourier Epicycles (Juan Carlos Ponce Campuzano, dynamicmath.xyz)
emulators.blurb: p5.js sketches that draw curves (a T-rex, a cat, logos) with concatenated rotating circles computed by the discrete Fourier transform.
emulators.why: A visually rich companion to the epicycle idea with the underlying math and references laid out beside the animations.
emulators.ease_note: Animations run on page load

emulators.name: Fractal Garden
emulators.blurb: An exhibition of 35 interactive fractals (2D, 3D and L-system) each with its own tweakable studio page and shareable settings.
emulators.why: The best single stop to sample many fractal families in a friendly, well-designed UI; the Barnsley fern page, for instance, lets you swap fern species and colours live.
emulators.ease_note: Pick a fractal, drag sliders, done

emulators.name: Fractal Lab (mirror)
emulators.blurb: Community-hosted mirror of Tom Beddard's Fractal Lab, the seminal WebGL 2D/3D fractal explorer with an in-browser GLSL shader editor.
emulators.why: Still one of the few tools that lets you edit the ray-marching shader directly and keep a library of your own fractals in local storage; the original subblue.com host is gone.
emulators.ease_note: Dense UI, and the author warns badly written shaders can lock up your GPU

emulators.name: Fractal Terrain Generator (qiao)
emulators.blurb: Three.js demo of the diamond-square algorithm generating random fractal terrain with size, smoothness and Z-scale controls.
emulators.why: A minimal, transparent implementation of the classic 1980s fractal-landscape algorithm you can regenerate endlessly.
emulators.ease_note: Three sliders and a Generate button

emulators.name: Fractal Visualizer (ggouzi)
emulators.blurb: Browser explorer covering Mandelbrot, Julia, Lyapunov and Newton fractals with presets, palettes and up-to-4K PNG export.
emulators.why: One of the few web tools with a proper Lyapunov fractal explorer alongside the usual suspects, and every configuration has a shareable link.
emulators.ease_note: Clear per-fractal pages with sliders; rendering at 4K can take a while

emulators.name: Free42 Web (HP-42S simulator)
emulators.blurb: A web shell around Thomas Okken's Free42, the widely used HP-42S re-implementation, compiled to run in the browser.
emulators.why: Gives you the full Free42 HP-42S engine (the same core as the SwissMicros DM42) with program execution, state management and mobile support, no download needed.
emulators.ease_note: Loads to a working calculator; larger WASM download on first visit.

emulators.name: GALe - Galaksija Emulator
emulators.blurb: A browser emulator of the Yugoslav Galaksija, a Z80 kit computer published in a magazine in 1983, with touch keyboard and a menu of programs.
emulators.why: Another magazine-published home-built computer, with its own BASIC; the site includes selectable games and a touch keyboard.
emulators.ease_note: Boots on load with visible program buttons.

emulators.name: GMT - Real-time 3D Fractal Explorer
emulators.blurb: WebGL2 3D fractal studio with real-time ray marching, path-traced final renders, keyframe animation and mesh/OpenVDB export.
emulators.why: Closest thing to Mandelbulber or Fragmentarium in a browser, with over 500 importable distance-estimator formulas and a community gallery.
emulators.ease_note: Professional-grade UI with a learning curve; wants a desktop GPU

emulators.name: Golly (web app)
emulators.blurb: The official Emscripten build of Golly, the canonical cellular-automata explorer, running in the browser with QuickLife, HashLife, JvN, Generations and RuleLoader algorithms.
emulators.why: If you want the real thing (von Neumann's universal constructor, Langton's loops, Codd, Wireworld, custom rule tables) without a download, this is the only place. Same menus and pattern collection as desktop Golly, updated for Golly 4.3 in 2024.
emulators.ease_note: Desktop-style UI is powerful but dense; some browser quirks with file dialogs. SourceForge blocks automated checks, so this one is unverified from our side.

emulators.name: Gravity Simulator (Harmony of the Spheres)
emulators.blurb: An n-body sandbox with real solar-system, exoplanet and spaceflight scenarios where you can add, edit and delete bodies.
emulators.why: Go beyond two-body orbits: run TRAPPIST-1, choreographed three-body solutions or colliding galaxies, or tweak the laws of physics and see what breaks.
can: add and edit planets and masses
emulators.ease_note: Click and run; 3-D needs WebGL

emulators.name: Gray-Scott Reaction-Diffusion (pmneila jsexp)
emulators.blurb: The widely-copied 2012 WebGL Gray-Scott simulation: paint on the canvas and watch solitons, worms, mazes and chaos emerge.
emulators.why: The original and still one of the fastest reaction-diffusion toys; twelve presets map the feed/kill parameter space and configs are shareable as strings.
emulators.ease_note: Draw and it evolves; needs WebGL float textures.

emulators.name: Growing Neural Cellular Automata (Distill)
emulators.blurb: Interactive Distill article where trained neural CA grow and regenerate emoji shapes in WebGL; erase parts and watch them heal.
emulators.why: A landmark demo of learned CA rules: damage the pattern with a click and see self-repair, switch models and rotate the perception field, all live in the page.
emulators.ease_note: Demo runs at the top of the article; just click on it.

emulators.name: Ham Radio School AM Simulator
emulators.blurb: Animates an RF carrier amplitude-modulated by tone generators or your own microphone, with carrier frequency, amplitude and time-speed controls.
emulators.why: Written for licence students, it lets you literally talk into an AM transmitter model and watch the envelope form.
can: modulate with tones or your voice
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load; mic optional

emulators.name: Ham Radio School FM Simulator
emulators.blurb: Companion to the AM simulator showing a carrier frequency-modulated by tones or microphone audio with adjustable deviation.
emulators.why: Makes deviation visible, which explains why over-deviated FM sounds distorted and splatters into adjacent channels.
can: modulate with tones or your voice
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load; mic optional

emulators.name: Ham Radio School FSK Digital Mode Simulator
emulators.blurb: Type text and watch it become an FSK waveform at a chosen baud rate and FSK order, with audio reference tones and live decoding readout.
emulators.why: Shows the anatomy of RTTY and FSK-style digital modes symbol by symbol, tying baud rate to bits per second.
emulators.ease_note: Type and press send

emulators.name: Ham Radio School HF Ionospheric Skip Visualizer
emulators.blurb: Simplified ray-trace of HF signals refracting off ionospheric layers with band, solar flux, time of day, takeoff angle and hop count controls plus a coverage map.
emulators.why: A rare browser propagation sim that shows skip distance and dead zones changing with frequency and time, useful for explaining band behaviour.
can: set solar flux and local time
place the transmitter by grid square
emulators.ease_note: Dropdowns and sliders

emulators.name: Ham Radio School Horizontal Dipole Visualizer
emulators.blurb: Rotatable 3-D mesh of a half-wave horizontal dipole's pattern that changes as you slide the height above ground from low to free space.
emulators.why: Answers the eternal question of how high a dipole should be by showing the lobes and takeoff angle change with height.
emulators.ease_note: One key slider

emulators.name: Ham Radio School Phased Array Visualizer
emulators.blurb: Top-down view of two phased verticals showing wave crests, nulls and the resulting azimuth pattern as spacing and phase difference change.
emulators.why: The classic two-vertical phased array for 40 and 80 m, made visual so cardioid and figure-eight patterns make sense.
can: toggle gain rays and pattern outline
emulators.ease_note: Two main sliders

emulators.name: Ham Radio School SWR Wave Simulator
emulators.blurb: Animates forward and reflected waves on a feedline and their sum, with a live SWR readout as you change the reflected amplitude.
emulators.why: Ties the abstract SWR number to the physical standing wave a mismatched antenna creates on coax.
emulators.ease_note: Sliders only

emulators.name: Ham Radio School Time & Frequency Domain FFT Analyzer
emulators.blurb: Side-by-side oscilloscope and spectrum analyser for microphone input or generated sine, square, sawtooth and sweep signals with selectable FFT size.
emulators.why: Demonstrates the time/frequency relationship and why a square wave has odd harmonics, using the signals hams actually deal with.
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load

emulators.name: Harmonics Explorer (Tero Parviainen)
emulators.blurb: Angular web app with a slider per harmonic that draws each partial and the summed waveform while playing the result.
emulators.why: Hands-on additive synth showing how harmonic content shapes a waveform, a direct analogue of spectral purity in transmitters.
can: set the amplitude of each harmonic
see individual partials and the sum
emulators.ease_note: Sliders and a play button

emulators.name: HexLife Explorer
emulators.blurb: A Rust/WebAssembly and WebGL2 explorer for hexagonal-grid automata with a ruleset editor, nine parallel worlds and auto-exploration.
emulators.why: Purpose-built for hex rules: an atlas of rules, analysis plots and shareable world codes make discovering hexagonal gliders easy.
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load; the many panels take a moment to grasp.

emulators.name: Hexular Studio
emulators.blurb: A JavaScript studio for creating and recording hexagonal cellular automata with 2-64 states, template rule builders and plugins.
emulators.why: Aimed at generative art: blend modes, fades and recording turn hex automata into animations, while the rule builders keep it approachable.
emulators.ease_note: Powerful but option-heavy; start from a preset.

emulators.name: Homebrew Hub (gbdev) - play Game Boy homebrew in the browser
emulators.blurb: gbdev's curated archive of over 1,500 community-made Game Boy, GBC, GBA and NES homebrew games and demos, each playable in-page through WebAssembly builds of binjgb, binjnes and mGBA.
emulators.why: All content is legal homebrew and demoscene work submitted by its authors, so you can browse, rate and play without ever touching a commercial ROM.
can: play in page via WASM emulators
emulators.ease_note: Click a game, press play.

emulators.name: HP-15C simulator by Greg Hewgill (web)
emulators.blurb: A browser build of Greg Hewgill's well-known HP-15C simulator, showing the full stack, storage registers and program mode.
emulators.why: Faithful HP-15C behaviour including complex numbers, matrices and keystroke programs, with source on GitHub; a PWA front end of the same core lives at elf.org/hp15c.
emulators.ease_note: Calculator loads immediately, keyboard usable.

emulators.name: HP-35 microcode emulator by Ashley Feniello
emulators.blurb: A bug-compatible JavaScript emulator that runs the actual HP-35 ROM microcode rather than mimicking its behaviour.
emulators.why: Reproduces the real firmware, including the famous early ROM bugs, so it behaves exactly like the original hardware.
emulators.ease_note: Loads directly as a calculator on screen.

emulators.name: HP-35 simulator by Neil Fraser
emulators.blurb: A live JavaScript simulation of the original 1972 HP-35 scientific RPN calculator, written to fill the gap in the HP Museum's simulator list.
emulators.why: Quick, faithful way to try classic HP RPN including the HP-35's original CHS quirk; source and graphics are downloadable as a ZIP.
emulators.ease_note: Page loads with a working calculator; just click the keys.

emulators.name: HP25u / HP21u / HP29u microcode emulators (Sydney-Smith)
emulators.blurb: Browser microcode emulators for the HP Woodstock-series HP-21, HP-25 and HP-29C (plus an HP-55u), derived from the author's HP67u engine.
emulators.why: Runs the real 1970s HP firmware in JavaScript, so program timing and edge cases match the physical calculators; sibling pages exist for hp21u, hp29u and hp55u.
emulators.ease_note: Direct link opens the working calculator.

emulators.name: HP67 Emulator by Greg Sydney-Smith
emulators.blurb: An HTML5 JavaScript emulator of the card-programmable HP-67 that is functionally equivalent to the original, with a state inspector and program control.
emulators.why: Lets you write and run HP-67 keystroke programs in the browser and peek at internal state; a microcode-based hp67u variant is also offered for purists.
emulators.ease_note: Click the run link on the page; calculator appears immediately.

emulators.name: IBM System/360 Model 50 microcode simulator
emulators.blurb: Ken Shirriff's browser simulator that executes the Model 50's actual microcode and drives an accurate, zoomable console with lights and roller displays.
emulators.why: Unique view inside a 1964 mainframe: step through individual microinstructions and watch registers, local store and console lights change.
emulators.ease_note: Press Run or Step; understanding what you see needs the accompanying blog post.

emulators.name: Ice Fractal Mandelbulb Viewer
emulators.blurb: GPU ray-traced Mandelbulb viewer with colour schemes, a Julia mode and URL sharing.
emulators.why: Adds a Julia-set mode and shareable links to the usual Mandelbulb tweaks, with a fast-controls mode that drops resolution while you drag.
emulators.ease_note: Obvious drag/scroll/pinch controls

emulators.name: Infinite Mac
emulators.blurb: Mihai Parparita's site that boots every classic Mac OS from System 1.0 through Mac OS X 10.4, plus NeXTSTEP, using Mini vMac, Basilisk II, SheepShaver, DingusPPC, Previous and PearPC compiled to WebAssembly.
emulators.why: The one-stop shop for the whole Apple/NeXT lineage: pre-loaded with period software, instant to start, and you can drag your own files or disk images in.
can: PowerPC Mac OS 9 and OS X
emulators.ease_note: Pick a year/OS and it boots to the desktop.

emulators.name: Inspiral Web
emulators.blurb: Nathan Friend's browser Spirograph: drag gears of different sizes inside or around rings to draw hypotrochoid patterns.
emulators.why: Feels exactly like the physical toy, with undo, gear visibility toggles and a gallery of other people's creations.
emulators.ease_note: Pick a gear and drag; desktop only

emulators.name: Intel 4004 emulator (e4004)
emulators.blurb: A JavaScript emulator, assembler and disassembler for the Intel 4004, the first commercial microprocessor, modelled on the virtual 6502 GUI.
emulators.why: Write 4-bit code for the 1971 chip that started it all and step through its registers and stack.
emulators.ease_note: Simple form-based interface; assembler syntax documented on page.

emulators.name: Interactive Fourier Transform Visualizer (stilesjesus)
emulators.blurb: React/Three.js app where you adjust wave frequencies and amplitudes and see the sum and its spectrum in 2-D or rotatable 3-D, with audio.
emulators.why: A modern 3-D take on the time/frequency relationship that is fun for demonstrations.
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load

emulators.name: Interactive Modulation Visualizer (Jesse Loewen)
emulators.blurb: Shows AM, FM and PM in both the time domain and the frequency domain, so you can watch sidebands multiply as the modulation index rises.
emulators.why: Directly visualises Carson's rule and AM overmodulation, both of which matter for keeping a signal clean and within bandwidth.
emulators.ease_note: Dropdown and sliders

emulators.name: Interactive Molecular Dynamics (Dan Schroeder)
emulators.blurb: A 2-D box of Lennard-Jones atoms you can heat, cool, squeeze and bond to watch solids, liquids and gases emerge.
emulators.why: Shows thermodynamics from the bottom up: temperature, pressure, phase changes and irreversibility from nothing but pairwise forces.
can: change atom count and box size
emulators.ease_note: Click and run

emulators.name: Interactive Voronoi Diagram Generator (WebGL)
emulators.blurb: Alex Beutel's WebGL Voronoi toy: click to add sites, animate them with user-written JavaScript motion functions, and export the data.
emulators.why: Uses the GPU cone-rendering trick so hundreds of moving sites stay smooth; writing your own motion function is a fun twist.
emulators.ease_note: Click and it works; motion scripting is optional

emulators.name: IQEngine
emulators.blurb: Browser-based SDR toolkit that renders spectrograms of IQ recordings (shared community captures or your own local files) with client-side FFT, filtering and analysis.
emulators.why: Lets you dig through real RF captures the way you would in an SDR program, with no install, and learn what signals look like in IQ form.
can: open local SigMF or raw IQ files
zoom the spectrogram and change FFT size
apply FIR filters and view time/frequency plots
emulators.ease_note: Powerful but assumes SDR familiarity

emulators.name: Ising Model Demo (Daniel Schroeder, Weber State)
emulators.blurb: Dan Schroeder's HTML5 canvas Ising simulation with grid sizes up to 500 and a temperature control.
emulators.why: Simple and fast; ideal for showing students domains forming as you sweep through the critical temperature.
emulators.ease_note: Adjust temperature and watch.

emulators.name: ising.js (Matt Bierbaum)
emulators.blurb: A 2D Ising model with Metropolis and Wolff cluster updates, temperature and field sliders, and live energy/magnetisation graphs.
emulators.why: Physics-grade: compare single-spin versus cluster algorithms near the critical temperature and download the measured data.
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load; graphs need a little physics context.

emulators.name: ISRM Virtual Slide Rule Simulators
emulators.blurb: The International Slide Rule Museum's gallery of JavaScript slide rule and calculator simulators, including Aristo rules with numeric cursor readout and the Curta simulator.
emulators.why: A single curated hub gathering Derek Ross's, Robert Wolf's and other simulators, with the Hemmi 266 electronics rule and MilDot Master among the oddities.
can: numeric cursor readout on Aristo rules
emulators.ease_note: Index page of simulators; no touch-device support on the older ones.

emulators.name: Jape - Javascript Psion Emulator (Organiser II)
emulators.blurb: Jaap Scherphuis' pure-JavaScript emulator of almost every Psion Organiser II model, with datapak/rampak support and snapshots.
emulators.why: Program in OPL on the 1986 Organiser II in your browser, load OPK pack images and save SNA snapshots; the whole thing is downloadable as a zip.
emulators.ease_note: Pick a model from a drop-down and it boots; packs are optional.

emulators.name: JavaScript Nascom 2 Emulator
emulators.blurb: Tommy Thorn's browser emulator of the British Nascom 2 kit computer with NAS-SYS 3 monitor and tape loading.
emulators.why: The Nascom was a classic 1979 Z80 kit sold to hobbyists; this runs it with NAS-SYS and lets you load .nas files.
emulators.ease_note: Boots to the monitor prompt; you need to know NAS-SYS commands.

emulators.name: JavaScript PDP 11/70 Emulator (Paul Nankervis)
emulators.blurb: A PDP-11/70 emulator in JavaScript that boots real operating systems such as Unix V5, 2.11BSD, RSTS/E, RSX-11M and RT-11 from disk images.
emulators.why: Log in to a genuine 1970s Unix or DEC operating system in seconds and see a working front panel with address and data lights.
can: boots Unix and DEC operating systems
emulators.ease_note: Choose an OS from the boot menu; some OSes need knowledge of their login and commands.

emulators.name: JP 48G RPN calculator (HP-48G clone) by Josh Poley
emulators.blurb: A workalike RPN calculator written in JavaScript that mimics the HP-48G's stack, directories, angle/base modes and key layout.
emulators.why: Lightweight alternative to a full Saturn emulator when you just want 48-style stack RPN with directories and modes in a browser tab.
emulators.ease_note: Page is the calculator; no setup.

emulators.name: JRPN (Jovial RPN) HP-16C / HP-15C simulator
emulators.blurb: A Flutter-built simulator of the HP-16C Computer Scientist and HP-15C that runs in the browser as well as on desktop and mobile.
emulators.why: Scalable vector UI, shareable calculator states encoded in the URL, and readable program import/export make it ideal for programmers who want a real 16C for bit twiddling.
emulators.ease_note: Landing page links to the web app for each model.

emulators.name: JS Mocha
emulators.blurb: Brad Grier's GWT port of his Mocha CoCo 2 emulator with a handful of his own 1980s Sandhill Colorsoft programs bundled.
emulators.why: A quick CoCo 2 that comes with legitimately licensed home-grown software and can mount cassettes or disks from a URL.
emulators.ease_note: Boots on load; simple menus.

emulators.name: js-dos (DOS.Zone Studio)
emulators.blurb: The js-dos DOSBox/DOSBox-X port to WebAssembly with a Studio page where you upload your own DOS program bundle and run it in the browser.
emulators.why: The de-facto standard for running DOS software on the web; Studio lets you package your own legally owned programs without writing code.
emulators.ease_note: You must bring a zip of a DOS program and answer a few packaging questions.

emulators.name: JS99'er
emulators.blurb: Rasmus Moustgaard's TI-99/4A emulator with a built-in software library, speech synthesis, disk and cassette support.
emulators.why: The best TI-99/4A on the web, boots to TI BASIC with Extended BASIC and a catalogue of freely distributable cartridges available from a menu.
emulators.ease_note: Boots to the TI title screen with a software dropdown.

emulators.name: jsbeeb
emulators.blurb: Matt Godbolt's cycle-accurate BBC Micro emulator with a large disc and tape catalogue, debugger and save states.
emulators.why: Boots straight into Elite, has a searchable library of freely available discs, and its debugger is superb for learning 6502; the canonical BBC Micro on the web.
emulators.ease_note: Boots immediately; menu bar makes loading discs obvious.

emulators.name: jsbeeb Acorn Atom edition
emulators.blurb: A fork of jsbeeb that adds the Acorn Atom, Acorn's 1980 predecessor to the BBC Micro.
emulators.why: Try Atom BASIC and its built-in assembler in a browser; the Atom is otherwise hard to find emulated online.
emulators.ease_note: Boots directly; same UI as jsbeeb.

emulators.name: jsEmu48 online HP-48GX emulator
emulators.blurb: An Emscripten port of Daniel Nilsson's HPEMU by Julien Meyer, billed as the first HP48G(X) emulator to run online, bundled with a game so it works out of the box.
emulators.why: Run real HP-48 Saturn code in the browser: push your own .var or .lib objects onto the stack at boot, remap keys and download snapshots for one-click replay.
emulators.ease_note: Starts running the bundled game immediately; loading your own files is optional.

emulators.name: JSLinux
emulators.blurb: Fabrice Bellard's TinyEMU-based emulator that boots Linux (and Windows 2000) on x86 and RISC-V machines in a browser tab.
emulators.why: Boot a full Linux with networking and a shell in seconds, or a 64-bit RISC-V system to try the architecture.
emulators.ease_note: Click a machine link and it boots to a shell.

emulators.name: JSSpeccy 3
emulators.blurb: Matt Westcott's third-generation ZX Spectrum emulator, rewritten in WebAssembly for accuracy and speed.
emulators.why: Accurate enough for demoscene timing tricks and trivially embeddable; the reference browser Spectrum from a well-known Spectrum demo coder.
emulators.ease_note: Boots to BASIC; loading software means opening your own files.

emulators.name: jsTIfied (Cemetech) TI-83+/TI-84+ emulator
emulators.blurb: Cemetech's in-browser Z80 TI graphing calculator emulator, integrated with the SourceCoder TI-BASIC editor.
emulators.why: Lets you test TI-BASIC and assembly programs from your own calculator's ROM image entirely in the browser, with everything stored locally.
emulators.ease_note: You must dump a ROM from a calculator you own before it will run.

emulators.name: JtyOne Online ZX81 Emulator
emulators.blurb: Simon Holdsworth's JavaScript port of the EightyOne emulator, hosted with the ZX81 Stuff software archive so programs load by name.
emulators.why: Boots to a blank ZX81 for typing in programs and can load hundreds of archived .p files directly, including hi-res graphics titles that need accurate timing.
can: LOAD programs by name from the archive
emulators.ease_note: Boots instantly; type LOAD "name" to run archive programs.

emulators.name: Julia Set Interactive Visualization
emulators.blurb: WebGL2 Julia set renderer where moving the mouse changes the parameter c in real time.
emulators.why: The most intuitive way to feel how Julia sets morph as c moves around the complex plane; click to freeze and save the image.
emulators.ease_note: Just move the mouse

emulators.name: Jupiter Ace Emulator
emulators.blurb: A browser emulator for the Forth-based Jupiter Ace with TAP/TZX loading, keyboard modes, speed control and beeper sound.
emulators.why: The only home computer that booted into Forth instead of BASIC; this site pairs the emulator with reference documentation.
emulators.ease_note: Boots to Forth; Forth itself is the learning curve.

emulators.name: Karl Sims RD Tool
emulators.blurb: Karl Sims' web app for growing reaction-diffusion textures with flow, orientation and colour controls on top of the Gray-Scott model.
emulators.why: Made by the artist behind the famous reaction-diffusion tutorial; the flow and anisotropy options produce zebra, coral and fingerprint textures you can't get from a plain simulator.
emulators.ease_note: Click a pattern and it grows; WebGL required.

emulators.name: L-Systems Turtle Graphics Renderer
emulators.blurb: Kevin Roast's HTML5 canvas L-system renderer with axiom, up to five production rules, angle and iteration controls and a preset gallery.
emulators.why: Simple and immediate for learning Lindenmayer systems: click a gallery thumbnail to load the rules, then edit them and re-render.
emulators.ease_note: Form-based but tiny and clear

emulators.name: Langton's Ant (ScienceDemos)
emulators.blurb: Dominic Ford's tidy Langton's ant demo that lets you flip squares, adjust speed, zoom and export the resulting highway as SVG.
emulators.why: A clean, explained implementation of the ant's chaos-then-highway behaviour, with presets and SVG export for illustrations.
emulators.ease_note: Press play; that's it.

emulators.name: Lenia (JavaScript)
emulators.blurb: Bert Chan's original browser implementation of Lenia, a continuous generalisation of Life with a taxonomy of dozens of life-like 'solitons'.
emulators.why: The canonical Lenia tool from its creator: load Orbium and friends, tweak kernel and growth parameters, and watch statistics and 3D plots update live.
emulators.ease_note: Dense control panel; pick a creature from the list to get going.

emulators.name: Let's Learn About Waveforms (Josh Comeau, The Pudding)
emulators.blurb: Interactive scrolling essay that introduces sine, square, saw and triangle waves, harmonics and phase with live audio and animated graphs.
emulators.why: Friendly on-ramp to the idea that timbre equals harmonic content, a foundation for reading spectra.
can: add harmonics one at a time
emulators.ease_note: Scroll and click

emulators.name: Life Universe (Life in Life)
emulators.blurb: An infinitely zoomable Game of Life in which each cell is itself a Game of Life built from OTCA metapixels, all the way down.
emulators.why: A jaw-dropping demonstration of Life's self-simulation: zoom out from a glider to discover it is a cell in a bigger glider. Great for showing why Life is Turing complete.
emulators.ease_note: Loads and runs by itself; just scroll to zoom.

emulators.name: LifeViewer
emulators.blurb: Chris Rowett's scriptable pattern viewer/editor used on the ConwayLife forums and LifeWiki, supporting an enormous range of rule families, neighbourhoods and grid topologies.
emulators.why: The most complete browser CA engine short of Golly: paste any RLE from LifeWiki, run non-totalistic, HROT or Margolus rules, step backwards, and annotate with its script language. Every LifeWiki pattern page embeds it.
emulators.ease_note: Paste RLE and press play; many keyboard shortcuts to learn.

emulators.name: LisaGUI
emulators.blurb: A faithful browser recreation of the Apple Lisa Office System desktop written from scratch in JavaScript; not a CPU emulator but a working reimplementation of the Lisa user interface.
emulators.why: There is no working Lisa emulator in a browser yet, and this is the closest thing: the real Lisa desktop metaphor, LisaWrite-style apps and quirks, running instantly.
can: boots to Lisa Office System desktop
emulators.ease_note: Opens straight to the desktop.

emulators.name: Little Man Computer
emulators.blurb: An animated browser implementation of the classic Little Man Computer teaching model with a von Neumann visualisation.
emulators.why: The standard model used in schools to explain fetch-decode-execute; watch the 'little man' move data between mailboxes.
emulators.ease_note: Click and it runs an example.

emulators.name: LogicEmu
emulators.blurb: Lode Vandevenne's ASCII-art-based logic simulator with built-in circuits ranging from gates to a working 8-bit CPU and a 16-bit computer.
emulators.why: Runs entirely locally with no server, includes remarkable prebuilt CPUs and a relay-logic mode, and circuits are just text you can edit.
emulators.ease_note: Browse the dropdown of circuits; editing needs the ASCII syntax.

emulators.name: Lorentz Transformation Web Simulator (ShareTechNote)
emulators.blurb: An interactive Minkowski diagram where a velocity slider skews the moving frame's grid and animates light clocks and photon pulses.
emulators.why: Watch space and time axes tilt as v approaches c, with split views for time dilation versus length contraction and simultaneity.
emulators.ease_note: Single page, click and drag

emulators.name: Lorenz Attractor (mathisonian)
emulators.blurb: A WebGL particle-system Lorenz attractor with a draggable camera and editable sigma, rho and beta constants in the text.
emulators.why: Change the constants in-line and watch the butterfly deform; a good quick visual for chaos talks.
emulators.ease_note: Runs on load; scrolling is a bit awkward.

emulators.name: Lotka Martini (Complexity Explorables)
emulators.blurb: A spatial predator-prey model on a hexagonal lattice showing Lotka-Volterra oscillations and activator-inhibitor waves.
emulators.why: Shows how population cycles emerge from local rules in space, with reproduction and death rates you can change mid-run.
emulators.ease_note: Press play.

emulators.name: Make Hyperbolic Tilings of Images
emulators.blurb: Malin Christersson's tool that tiles the Poincaré disc with an image using any {p,q} regular hyperbolic tiling and exports hi-res results.
emulators.why: Turns any picture into an Escher Circle Limit-style artwork, with a choice of Klein or polynomial distortion for the base tile.
emulators.ease_note: Upload, pick p/q, generate; large exports can crash Chrome

emulators.name: Mandelbrot & Co
emulators.blurb: Multi-core JavaScript explorer for eight escape-time fractal families with guided points of interest, filters and zoom-video creation.
emulators.why: Handy for people who want to explore beyond the plain Mandelbrot set: Burning Ship, Multibrots and a Collatz fractal are all a click away, with edge-detection and 3D-shading filters.
emulators.ease_note: Wheel/touch zoom; many options but clearly labelled

emulators.name: Mandelbrot Set Explorer (mandel.gart.nz)
emulators.blurb: Street-map style real-time Mandelbrot explorer with Julia set previews, animated palettes and 4K poster downloads.
emulators.why: The scroll/zoom feel is unusually smooth and natural, and permanent links plus 4K exports make it a good choice for making wall art.
emulators.ease_note: Behaves like a web map; no setup

emulators.name: Mandelbrot Set Explorer (WebGPU)
emulators.blurb: Real-time WebGPU Mandelbrot renderer with perturbation-based arbitrary-precision deep zoom, bookmarks and gradient editing.
emulators.why: A showcase of what WebGPU can do for fractals; deep zooms stay fluid, and bookmarks plus local-storage settings make it easy to come back to a spot.
emulators.ease_note: Needs a WebGPU-capable browser (Chrome/Edge 113+); otherwise drag and scroll

emulators.name: Mandelbrot Viewer (David Eck)
emulators.blurb: Classic educational Mandelbrot viewer from David Eck's textbook site with box zoom, palette editor and XML save/load.
emulators.why: Very transparent and teachable: choose iteration counts up to 50,000, edit palettes by hue/saturation/brightness, and save your examples as XML.
emulators.ease_note: Drag a box to zoom; lots of menus but all self-explanatory

emulators.name: mandelbrot.site
emulators.blurb: Rust-to-WebAssembly Mandelbrot viewer built on a Leaflet map-style interface with arbitrary-precision perturbation deep zoom.
emulators.why: Feels like Google Maps for the Mandelbrot set, and it is a PWA so it works offline; PNG exports embed the parameters so any image can be reopened later.
emulators.ease_note: Scroll to zoom like a web map; everything else is optional

emulators.name: Mandelbulb.xyz
emulators.blurb: WebGL real-time Mandelbulb explorer with adjustable power, iterations, materials and animation, plus a view-the-shader option.
emulators.why: Zero-friction way to spin a Mandelbulb around on desktop or phone and see how the power parameter changes its shape.
emulators.ease_note: Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom

emulators.name: Mandelscope
emulators.blurb: WebGL Mandelbrot and Julia explorer that switches to perturbation rendering (Decimal.js reference orbits) for zooms down to about 1e-38.
emulators.why: Good middle ground between simple viewers and hardcore deep zoomers, with auto-iteration tuning, orbit-quality feedback and preset locations such as Seahorse Valley.
emulators.ease_note: Drag, scroll and pinch just work; advanced settings are optional

emulators.name: MARIE.js
emulators.blurb: A JavaScript simulator for the MARIE educational computer architecture from Null and Lobur's textbook, with datapath visualisation.
emulators.why: Runs the textbook exercises with a live datapath view and stepping, no Java required unlike the original MarieSim.
emulators.ease_note: Obvious editor and run controls.

emulators.name: Marki Microwave LC Filter Design Tool
emulators.blurb: Web application that synthesizes Butterworth, Chebyshev, Elliptic, Bessel and Legendre LC filters up to 20th order and plots insertion loss, return loss, phase and group delay.
emulators.why: Design harmonic low-pass and band-pass filters for a homebrew transmitter with real E-series values and export to LTspice or Qucs.
emulators.ease_note: Free, but a dense engineering form

emulators.name: Matter.js Demo Playground
emulators.blurb: Interactive demos of the Matter.js rigid-body engine: stacks, chains, bridges, cloth, Newton's cradle and more you can grab and throw.
emulators.why: A browser stand-in for desktop physics sandboxes; every demo is live and draggable and the engine source is open.
emulators.ease_note: Click and grab

emulators.name: micro:bit Python Editor (with simulator)
emulators.blurb: The official micro:bit Python editor with a built-in simulator that runs the real MicroPython firmware and lets you press buttons, tilt and use sensors.
emulators.why: Runs actual micro:bit firmware compiled to WebAssembly, so code behaves exactly as on the board.
emulators.ease_note: Open, type Python, press play on the simulator.

emulators.name: MicroPython on Unicorn (pyboard simulator)
emulators.blurb: The official MicroPython site's in-browser pyboard simulator, running MicroPython on an emulated ARM Cortex-M via the Unicorn engine with virtual LEDs, servo, ADC and I2C LCD.
emulators.why: Try MicroPython hardware scripts (pyb module, LEDs, servo) with no board, choosing RAM, stack and clock speed to see how constraints bite.
can: virtual LEDs, servo, ADC and LCD
emulators.ease_note: Click Run on the sample script; older page but still functional.

emulators.name: MIT Mathlets: Bode and Nyquist Plots
emulators.blurb: Drag poles and zeros in the s-plane and watch Bode and Nyquist plots of the transfer function update live.
emulators.why: Connects pole positions to frequency response and phase margin, the mental model behind filter and PLL design.
emulators.ease_note: Poles are placed by dragging, no formula entry

emulators.name: MIT Mathlets: Convolution, Flip and Drag
emulators.blurb: MIT Mathlet where you drag the time-reversed impulse response across a signal and watch the weighted integral build the convolution.
emulators.why: Clean, authoritative HTML5 visual of convolution from MIT's differential equations courses.
can: see the product and accumulated integral
emulators.ease_note: Sliders only

emulators.name: MIT Mathlets: Fourier Coefficients
emulators.blurb: Slide individual Fourier coefficients to fit a target periodic function and see how symmetry decides which harmonics are needed.
emulators.why: Hands-on feel for sine versus cosine terms and the RMS best fit, complementing the Falstad and PhET tools.
can: compare partial sums to the target
emulators.ease_note: Sliders only

emulators.name: MMBasic Anywhere Web (PicoMite / PicoCalc emulator)
emulators.blurb: A WebAssembly port of the PicoMite MMBasic interpreter and its bytecode VM that runs PicoCalc-style BASIC programs in the browser with a virtual SD card and built-in editor.
emulators.why: Lets you write and test MMBasic programs for the ClockworkPi PicoCalc without flashing hardware or swapping SD cards, with a fast edit-run loop and PicoCalc-like screen sizes.
can: virtual SD card with drag-and-drop files
emulators.ease_note: Open the page, type BASIC or drop a .bas file, press run.

emulators.name: Moonjs Apollo Guidance Computer
emulators.blurb: An Emscripten port of Virtual AGC running the real Colossus 249 flight software from Apollo 9 behind a clickable DSKY.
emulators.why: Enter Verb/Noun commands exactly as the astronauts did and watch the actual flight code respond; no install of Virtual AGC required.
emulators.ease_note: Click and it runs; you need a cheat sheet of verbs and nouns, which the page provides.

emulators.name: My TRS-80
emulators.blurb: Lawrence Kesteloot's web app that hosts a virtual TRS-80 with a personal library of cassettes and floppy images.
emulators.why: Beyond emulation it keeps your program library in the browser and can decode real cassette audio; part of an open TypeScript TRS-80 toolkit.
emulators.ease_note: Full-featured app with a library concept that takes a minute to understand.

emulators.name: myFourierEpicycles
emulators.blurb: Draw a shape with the mouse or upload an SVG and watch a chain of rotating circles (a DFT) redraw it, 3Blue1Brown style.
emulators.why: Makes the complex Fourier coefficients tangible as amplitude/phase/frequency of spinning vectors, the same objects behind IQ signals.
emulators.ease_note: Just draw on the canvas

emulators.name: myPhysicsLab
emulators.blurb: About fifty real-time classical-mechanics simulations with editable parameters, live graphs and the underlying equations explained.
emulators.why: A physics-lab style sandbox: drag objects mid-simulation, plot any variable against any other, and read the math behind each model.
can: edit masses, springs, gravity and damping
emulators.ease_note: Click and run

emulators.name: MZ-700 Full JavaScript Emulator
emulators.blurb: Takamin's HTML5 emulator of the Sharp MZ-700 'clean computer' with its monitor ROM and cassette loading.
emulators.why: A rarely emulated Japanese 8-bit that shipped with only a monitor; you load BASIC from tape just as owners did.
emulators.ease_note: Boots to the monitor; you need an MZT of BASIC to do much.

emulators.name: Nand2Tetris Web IDE
emulators.blurb: The official browser IDE for the Nand2Tetris course: hardware simulator, Hack CPU emulator, VM emulator and assembler.
emulators.why: Build a computer from NAND gates upward and run your own CPU, entirely in the browser with no Java tools.
emulators.ease_note: Multiple tools; follow the course to make sense of them.

emulators.name: NandGame
emulators.blurb: A puzzle game where you build a working computer from a single NAND gate, through ALU, memory and CPU, to programming it.
emulators.why: The Turing Complete style experience free in a browser; each level is a live logic simulation you wire yourself.
emulators.ease_note: Drag components and connect; guided by levels.

emulators.name: NanoWasp (MicroBee)
emulators.blurb: A JavaScript emulator of the Australian MicroBee with BASIC in ROM.
emulators.why: The MicroBee was Australia's school computer and a kit-built favourite; NanoWasp boots it to BASIC in any browser.
emulators.ease_note: Boots on load; note the site is plain http.

emulators.name: NASA Eyes on the Solar System
emulators.blurb: NASA/JPL's 3-D solar system where you fly to planets, moons and spacecraft and scrub time forward and back.
emulators.why: Official mission geometry in the browser: follow Voyager, JWST or Mars rovers with real trajectory data and speed up time to watch orbits.
emulators.ease_note: Click and explore; needs WebGL

emulators.name: NERDfirst Nyquist Theorem Simulator
emulators.blurb: A two-panel simulator showing an original wave and its sampled reconstruction with a live verdict on whether the sample rate exceeds twice the signal frequency.
emulators.why: The simplest possible aliasing demo, good for explaining Nyquist to a club audience in thirty seconds.
emulators.ease_note: Two sliders

emulators.name: NetLogo Web
emulators.blurb: The browser version of NetLogo with its full Models Library: Sugarscape, Ants, Wolf Sheep Predation, Fire, Flocking, Segregation, B-Z Reaction and hundreds more.
emulators.why: One site covers most of the classic emergence models with editable source, so you can read and modify the rules of Sugarscape or the BZ reaction instead of just watching.
emulators.ease_note: Open File > Models Library and search; the IDE is a bit heavy.

emulators.name: Newton-Raphson Fractal Explorer
emulators.blurb: WebGL explorer for generalised Newton fractals of real-coefficient polynomials up to degree 9, with animation across parameters.
emulators.why: Goes deeper than most Newton toys: vary the relaxation parameter alpha or the seed and animate through extra dimensions of the fractal.
emulators.ease_note: Powerful but the author admits the control docs are unfinished

emulators.name: Nova Emulator in Browser (NovaJS)
emulators.blurb: A browser-based Data General Nova emulator with front panel, teletype, disk and tape peripherals, and preloaded diagnostics, DOS and Spacewar.
emulators.why: The Nova is rarely emulated online; this one lets you flip the switches and boot period operating systems from a real DG software collection.
